title: Astrid and the Wolf
premise: Oscar Ishikawa, a memory-thief and ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, is pressed into service by a dying stranger who leaves him a map to the Vault of Unremembered Kings — the resting place of a truth that once ended an ancient war by erasing it from every mind alive. Hunted by both the guild, which wants the secret sold, and the Crown's inquisitors, who want it buried again, Oscar flees with Astrid Vane, a disgraced knight called 'the Wolf' whose own erased memories are the key to opening the vault. As their uneasy alliance deepens into loyalty, Oscar must choose between returning Astrid's stolen past to her — which will reignite the war — or keeping her ignorant and safe. In the end he gives her back her memories, she chooses peace over vengeance, and together they burn the map, trading truth for a future neither can fully remember.
about_author: Orsen Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city he still refuses to name. He writes fantasy about people who keep dangerous records, and claims his best ideas come from documents that were supposed to be destroyed.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Oscar Ishikawa's POV. In the guildhall of the Guild of Impossible Things, Oscar balances ledgers that record traded memories, bottled storms, and stolen years. He is careful, invisible, and quietly ashamed of what he keeps. The beat establishes his complicity: he tells himself bookkeeping is not thieving.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses into Oscar's counting room, presses a wax-sealed map into his hands, and dies whispering the word 'Astrid.' Guild enforcers arrive minutes behind him. Oscar hides the map inside a false ledger page. The beat is fear hardening into a terrible decision.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Summoned before Guildmaster Corvane, Oscar lies about the stranger while watching Corvane buy a soldier's memory of a massacre. Oscar realizes the guild doesn't just trade memories — it curates history. The beat is dawning horror at how deep his complicity runs.

chapters.title: The Wolf of Ashgate
chapters.summary: Astrid Vane's POV. Introduce Astrid, a disgraced knight working as a bounty hunter, haunted by gaps in her memory and a wolf-shaped scar she cannot explain. She is hired to find a thief who stole from the guild. The beat is her restless suspicion that she has been robbed of herself.

chapters.title: Two Thieves, One Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid corners Oscar in a smuggler's inn; instead of turning him in, she finds the map on him and recognizes the seal — it matches a fragment of memory that surfaces unbidden. They strike a wary bargain. The beat is reluctant alliance between two liars.

chapters.title: The Road Through Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Traveling through a village where no one remembers their own children, Astrid realizes whole communities have been 'harvested.' Oscar confesses the guild's role. She nearly abandons him; instead she punches him and keeps walking. The beat is fury transmuting into shared purpose.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV (the antagonist). The Crown's chief inquisitor interrogates the guildmaster, revealing the Crown erased the ancient war deliberately and will kill to keep it forgotten. Hale is not cruel — he sincerely believes forgetting saved millions. The beat is chilling, sympathetic conviction.

chapters.title: Memories for Sale
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. To fund the journey, Oscar does the one thing he swore off: steals a memory himself, taking a dying woman's last summer at her family's request. He feels the weight of what he carries — literally, now, in his own head. The beat is guilt becoming understanding.

chapters.title: The First Key
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Following the map to a drowned chapel, Astrid touches the altar and a memory floods back: she was the war's last witness, its memories sealed inside her. She tells Oscar nothing. The beat is terror — she now knows why everyone wants her.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ferry
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Guild enforcers ambush them at a river crossing; Astrid discovers Oscar secretly copied the map as insurance for a deal with Corvane. She leaves him bleeding on the bank. The beat is betrayal cutting deeper because it was half-expected.

chapters.title: Alone with the Truth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Captured by Hale, Oscar is shown the full archive of the erased war — cities, names, a peace bought with universal amnesia. Hale offers him a choice: help bury it forever, or die with it. The beat is seduction of a comfortable lie.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Alone, Astrid recovers more fragments: she chose the erasure once before, sacrificing her own past to seal the vault. She realizes Oscar's copy of the map is the only backup of her decision. The beat is grief meeting resolve.

chapters.title: The Prisoner's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar escapes Hale using a stolen memory as a weapon — making the inquisitor briefly feel the war's horror. Shaken, Hale lets him go rather than report failure. The beat is mercy born of shared trauma, complicating the antagonist.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Snow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Oscar tracks Astrid through mountain passes and offers her the copied map freely, confessing everything. She takes it but doesn't forgive him. They travel on in silence that slowly thaws. The beat is trust rebuilt brick by cold brick.

chapters.title: The Guild Closes Its Hand
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guildmaster, revealed to be one of the original architects of the erasure, mobilizes everything to reach the vault first — he intends to sell the war's secrets to the highest bidder among old noble houses. The beat is banal, commercial evil.

chapters.title: Descent to the Vault
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Guided by her returning memories, Astrid leads Oscar beneath the ruined capital to the Vault of Unremembered Kings, pursued by both guild and Crown. The vault opens only to her blood and her consent. The beat is dread and awe in equal measure.

chapters.title: The War Beneath the World
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inside, they experience the war as preserved memory: not heroes and monsters but ordinary people on both sides, and a peace signed in mutual forgetting. Astrid understands her old self's choice completely. The beat is devastating empathy.

chapters.title: Corvane's Auction
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corvane arrives with enforcers and noble buyers, intending to strip the vault and sell selective truths that would reignite the war profitably. Oscar, the ledger-keeper, publicly reads aloud the guild's own accounts of every atrocity it enabled. The beat is the clerk finally testifying.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Wolf
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. With the vault open, Astrid holds the power to restore the war's truth to the world — and with it, every old grievance. Remembering her sacrifice, she chooses instead to complete the erasure, this time willingly and with witnesses. The beat is agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Hale arrives not to stop them but to help burn the vault, having been changed by Oscar's stolen memory. Corvane fights; Astrid defeats him without killing, and the guild's ledgers burn alongside the vault. The beat is cathartic destruction of corrupt institutions.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the aftermath, Oscar returns every memory he ever stole or kept, including the ones Astrid entrusted to him. He keeps only one: not hers, but his own memory of her, which no one asked him to surrender. The beat is quiet, chosen love.

chapters.title: Astrid and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. Months later, Astrid — her past gone but her future her own — finds Oscar keeping honest accounts for a village school. Neither remembers everything they were to each other, but both keep choosing each other anyway. The beat is bittersweet peace: some things survive even forgetting.
